read: A risk-off week ended with a regulatory jolt. XBI fell 2.7% on Friday to $140.18, about 6.9% down on the week and near a 60-session low, as the tape traded macro (Fed-hike repricing) more than news. The biggest stock-specific event was the FDA's second CRL for Capricor's deramiocel. An unusual public FDA statement cited data-integrity failures in HOPE-3, and CAPR fell about 80% after hours. Taken with Savara's missed PDUFA and last week's ivonescimab CRL, the agency is enforcing process and evidentiary standards rather than leaning into rare-disease flexibility. On the positive side, Merck's Kelun-sourced TROP2 ADC sac-TMT hit OS in later-line gastroesophageal cancer, and the pan-RAS race tightened as Erasca's ERAS-0015 posted a 44% confirmed ORR in 2L+ PDAC. Capital is still going to China-originated, de-risked oncology even as Congress argues over restricting US money flowing the other way. The weekend itself was quiet.

items.headline: Merck & Co: sac-TMT (Kelun-Biotech TROP2 ADC) meets OS in Phase 3 TroFuse-015, 3L+ gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma
items.detail: n=473 vs physician's choice. OS was significant and consistent regardless of TROP2 expression, but PFS missed and ORR was not formally tested; no numbers yet. It is the second global Phase 3 win from 18 TroFuse studies (after endometrial at ESMO). BMO models $4.3bn peak, central to Merck's Keytruda LOE (end-2028) replacement plan. It is the first TROP2 ADC with OS in this setting, ahead of Gilead's Trodelvy and AstraZeneca/Daiichi Sankyo's Datroway. Endometrial PDUFA by June 2027.

items.headline: Capricor: second FDA CRL for deramiocel in DMD; FDA cites serious HOPE-3 data-integrity violations
items.detail: CAPR fell about 80% after hours on Friday to $1.63 (from a $7.59 close). The FDA issued a rare public statement listing unauthorised post-hoc SAP changes, blinding breaches and other protocol violations that make HOPE-3 data unreliable and impossible to fix post hoc, plus a Regulatory Responsibility Letter. The pivot to an upper-limb indication did not help. Cash is about $198.5m (runway of 12+ months). Company call is today at 8:30am ET. The read-across to other DMD sponsors is limited because the problem was trial conduct, not the evidence bar.

items.headline: Erasca: ERAS-0015 (oral pan-RAS molecular glue) Phase 1 update: 44% confirmed ORR in 2L+ KRAS G12X PDAC
items.detail: At 32 mg QD: n=25; 69% confirmed ORR in G12D/G12V (n=13); all 11 responders still on drug; no DLTs. The 1L PDAC Phase 3 is pulled forward to 1H27. Shares fell 5% on small n, no durability and no chemo-combo efficacy. Read-across to Revolution Medicines: Rasonque's 1L PDAC combo data a day earlier showed 60.7% ORR and 12.8-month PFS (n=61). Truist argues ORR alone will not dent Rasonque's randomized OS advantage. ERAS-0015 is in-licensed from China's Joyo Pharmatech.

items.headline: Savara: FDA will miss the 22 November PDUFA for molgramostim (Molbreevi) in autoimmune PAP, with no new date
items.detail: SVRA fell 18% to $4.26. This follows an April three-month extension. Jefferies reads it as FDA bandwidth, not a hidden CRL, keeps high approval confidence and models $500m+ peak sales. It is a rare missed PDUFA.

items.headline: Policy: bipartisan draft letters pull Treasury's China biotech outbound-investment rules in both directions
items.detail: Lawmakers in both chambers are lobbying Treasury to loosen or tighten draft limits on US investment in Chinese biotech before final rules, ahead of a Democrat-led Congress. This is the key overhang for the China-licensing trade (sac-TMT, ERAS-0015 and last week's Pfizer/Starna are all China-sourced).

items.headline: Market: XBI down about 6.9% on the week to $140.18, near a 60-session low
items.detail: Friday alone was -2.7%. One recap had biotech outperforming a sharper S&P 500 decline. The sell-off was macro-led, with rising Fed-hike expectations.

items.headline: Novo: 215 more job cuts at its US HQ as part of a sales reorganisation
items.detail: This continues the Doustdar cost programme as Wegovy-pill scripts soften against Lilly's Foundayo.

items.headline: BioNTech: about 40 further cuts at its Mainz HQ
items.detail: These come on top of about 1,800 already earmarked elsewhere. 2026 revenue guidance was lifted to €1.7-1.9bn with Q3; JPM nudged its target to $93 (Neutral).

items.headline: Neumirna Therapeutics: up to €12.5m EIC Accelerator award for anti-miRNA NMT.001 in drug-resistant epilepsy
items.detail: Non-dilutive funding to take it into Phase 1/2.
